item.title: Gardaí carried out over 4,100 checkpoints in Kerry last year
item.description: Gardaí in Kerry carried out 4,180 checkpoints in the county last year. Nationally last year, Gardaí carried out over 100,000 checkpoints; over 51,000 were mandatory intoxicant testing checkpoints, while the remainder were classed as other and truck/HGV checkpoints. In the first two weeks of this year, Gardaí nationwide carried out more than 3,500 checkpoints and 130 of those were in Kerry. item.title: Applications are open for Culture Night Late 2026
item.description: Applications are now open for events and workshops in the Kingdom, as part of Culture Night 2026. Culture Night Late provides funding for late-night Culture Night events and activities, and focuses on the key role of the arts in cultivating a vibrant and inclusive night-time economy in Ireland. Now in it's 21st year, Culture Night is an annual initiative by the Arts Council of Ireland to celebrate the arts, culture, and music all over Ireland. item.title: France defeat Italy
item.description: France remain on course for a rugby union Six Nations Grand Slam. They scored five tries as they comfortably beat Italy 33-8 in Lille. France are top of the standings with three victories from three matches, while Italy are fifth only above winless Wales. Advertisement

item.title: NHL review
item.description: Kilkenny needed a late winner to see off Waterford in Division 1A of the National Hurling League. Cian Kenny's free completed a comeback for the Cats who came away from Nowlan Park with a 1-21 to 1-20 victory. Meanwhile, Galway have their first win of the year. Advertisement They were too good for Offaly and emerged as 2-23 to 18 point winners.

item.title: Celtic beaten
item.description: Both Old Firm clubs have lost ground in the Scottish Premiership title race. Rangers are four points behind leaders Hearts after drawing 2?2 at bottom side Livingston -despite facing ten men late on. Celtic also slipped up, losing 2?1 at home to Hibs after they conceded a late goal and a red card for Auston Trusty. Advertisement The champions are six points off the top, but do have a game in hand.

item.title: NFL review
item.description: Donegal have kept up their unbeaten run in Division 1 of the National Football League. They had no problems against Armagh, coming out on top with a 1-20 to 19 point win. Meanwhile Monaghan's search for a first win goes on. Advertisement They fell to a 2-30 to 2-11 loss at home to Mayo. Kobe McDonald, son of Mayo great Ciaran, scored 1-4 off the bench in that game.

item.title: Killarney's Jessie Buckley wins Leading Actress at 2026 BAFTAs in historic first for Ireland
item.description: Jessie Buckley has won the Leading Actress award at the 2026 BAFTA Film Awards in London for her performance in Hamnet. The Killarney star becomes the first Irish actress to take the top honour in the category at the main BAFTA Film Awards. She was presented with the award by previous BAFTA winner Cillian Murphy, who is part of an ambitious project to reinvigorate the Phoenix Cinema in Dingle.. item.title: Foo Fighters play secret gig in Dingle
item.description: Foo Fighters have played a secret gig in Dingle to mark the 25th year anniversary of the founding of the Other Voices festival. The concert was held in St James' Church - the venue synonymous with Other Voices. The gig was filmed for Other Voices. Advertisement The Irish Times has described the concert performed by one of the world's biggest bands in a venue that can only seat around 80 as 'euphoric'.
